newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Air France in profit, seeks to privatise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Air France in profit, seeks to privatise.

text.p: French state carrier Air France said on Thursday it made a small profit last year, its first since 1989, and the airline's management renewed a plea for privatisation.

The centre-right government has slated the airline for sale to the private sector but the cloud of a parliamentary election hangs over the plan. The left-wing parties are in with a chance of power on Sunday after winning the first round vote.
Air France reported a net consolidated profit of 394 million francs ($68.5 million), despite a loss of 250 million francs due to strikes, managing director Patrice Durand told reporters.

The result includes profits from subsidiaries like Servair, Air Charter and Jet Tour but not short- and medium-haul airline Air France Europe -- otherwise known as Air Inter -- which was to publish separate results later on Thursday.
Air France made a consolidated loss of 2.264 billion francs in the preceding financial year, to end-March 1996.
Durand said he hoped Air France would be "a bit more than at breakeven" at the end of a 1997/98 financial year in which its Air France Europe unit will be merged with the parent group.

The recovery from years of losses in the 1996/97 financial year showed the airline had the potential to catch up on leaders like British Airways and should not miss out on the chance to privatise, he told a pre-results news conference.

"We are a public enterprise but one which lives in a totally competitive world just like goods and services companies. Economic logic weighs heavily in favour of privatisation," Durand told reporters.

"The return to breakeven shows Air France has the ability to capitalise on its qualities. We believe that if we don't make too many errors we could be up there close to British Airways in a few years," Durand told reporters.
"We have a wonderful new episode within our reach but it would be a shame to leave it dangling there and never seize the chance."

The airline said consolidated turnover in the year to March 31 rose to 46.4 billion francs from 43.23 billion a year earlier and that operating profit leapt to 1.14 billion francs from 420 million in the 1995/96 financial year.

The airline said turnover in the past financial year rose mainly due to a rise of 2.7 billion francs in passenger and baggage revenues. Passenger operations posted 13.3 percent growth, it said. On the freight side, there was a 5.5 percent increase in traffic.
The airline said fuel costs increased 1.2 billion francs.

Losses due to strikes in the 1996/97 year amounted to 250 million francs. This year its results will have to account for another 200 million which Durand said was the estimated cost of strikes earlier this month by pilots fighting lower pay scales.

While the Socialist party has challenged the centre-right's privatisation policy, it is still sending mixed signals on the extent to which it would actually halt sell-offs and appears to be keeping an open mind at least as far as partial stake sales are concerned. ($ = 5.749 French Francs)
